title: Plate Containment Orientation Search
status: DEVELOPMENT / NON-CANON / EXPLORATORY FAILURE TO FIND A COMMON ROTATION

method.sphereRotation: One common 3D rotation applied to all six continent footprints; Euler rotations in XYZ order.
method.projection: Inverse of the plate baseline's inverse-stereographic projection: x = X/(1-Z), y = Y/(1-Z).
method.containment: A continent sample point must lie inside its assigned bounded plate-face polygon. Central is treated as the complementary spherical face, so its sample points must lie outside the outer polygon.
method.sampling: Every sixth rendered SVG vertex, approximately two samples per original coastline edge.
method.search: 40,000 deterministic pseudo-random global rotations using fixed seed 20261118; also checked a coarse 30-degree Euler grid.
method.interpretation: This is a search for a shared global orientation, not an exhaustive proof that no orientation exists. Sample-point containment is a screening test; it does not replace exact polygon-edge intersection and full spherical topology validation.

decision.conclusion: V0.6 continent area targets fit below the nominal area of their assigned carrier plates, but the present continent placements and V1.0-R plate partition have not been reconciled by a common globe rotation.
decision.notProven: This search does not prove that a valid orientation is mathematically impossible.
nextSteps: Do not describe continent containment as passed.
Choose whether to preserve the current continent macro-layout or preserve the current plate partition as the stronger design constraint.
If preserving the plate partition, redesign continent placement within carrier faces while retaining area targets and checking inter-continent separation.
If preserving continent placement, revise the plate graph geometry/topology or carrier-face assignment and revalidate spherical plate areas.
After a candidate is found, run exact spherical polygon containment and boundary-intersection tests rather than relying on samples.
